result.summary: Implemented REQ-050 per lib/letflow/design/req050-exclusive-gateway-cel.md. Created lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex (Letflow.Engine.Expr): translate_cel_to_expr/1 (strips 'variables.' prefix, '&&'->'and', '||'->'or', '!'->'not ' with '!=' passing through unchanged via negative-lookahead regex; detects the 4 unsupported-CEL-feature categories -- macros, type-conversion functions, collection functions/'in', ternary '?' -- string-literal-aware, before any rewrite), parse/1 (hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser over the or/and/not/cmp/operand grammar), eval/2 (walks the AST against a variables map; undefined variable and type-mismatch are eval errors; ==/!= never error across mismatched types; </<=/>/>= require both operands numeric), and evaluate_condition/2 (the always-boolean catch-false composition of the three: any error at any stage, or a non-true {:ok, _} result, uniformly yields false). Rewrote dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, replacing the {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, node_id} stub at the old transition.ex:256-259: partitions the gateway's outgoing edges into conditioned_edges (declared order) and at-most-one default_edge (relying on REQ-029's CHK-13..CHK-16 invariants, not re-validated); walks conditioned_edges in declared order calling Expr.evaluate_condition/2, short-circuiting on the first true match and advancing the token onto that edge's target; if none match, falls back unconditionally to the default edge if present (never evaluated as a condition, evaluated last by construction regardless of its declared position); if neither matches, returns {:error, {:no_matching_edge, node.id, evaluated_conditions}} where evaluated_conditions is one %{edge_id, condition, result: false} entry per conditioned edge in declared order, condition always the original CEL string. Extended Transition.transition_error/0 with the :no_matching_edge variant and added the evaluated_condition/0 type, per the design's §3. Updated the module's moduledoc paragraph describing which node types REQ-044 vs REQ-050 own. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: 'Compiling 2 files (.ex)\nGenerated letflow app' -- exit 0, zero warnings. mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex: exit 0 after running mix format on both files (2 pre-existing unrelated files -- test/letflow/event_store_test.exs, lib/letflow/identity_migration.ex, test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs -- were already unformatted on this branch before my change, confirmed via git stash; left untouched, out of scope). No priv/repo/migrations/*.exs added -- pure module, no DB. Purity grep (Repo.|Logger.|DateTime.|System.os_time|System.system_time|HTTPoison|Req.|File.|:rand.|:crypto.) over instance_state.ex/token.ex/transition.ex/expr.ex: all matches are inside @moduledoc prose (the purity-contract description text and its own embedded grep-command example), identical in kind to matches already present in the REQ-044-shipped transition.ex on main before this change (confirmed via git show HEAD) -- zero matches in actual code bodies/call graphs. Logically walked all 8 ACs against the implementation: declared-order + default-last (edges partitioned before any evaluation, default excluded from the ordering loop by construction); catch-false on both runtime errors and unsupported CEL features (single evaluate_condition/2 composition, one uniform catch-false, no separate branches); no-match-no-default error tuple names node_id and evaluated_conditions (edge_id/condition/result per entry); exactly-one-edge (match short-circuits the loop, default is mutually exclusive with a match, error path takes zero edges); all 4 translateCelToExpr rewrites implemented as specified with the != carve-out; zero I/O confirmed by grep+read. KNOWN FALLOUT (not fixed by me, TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3 scope per this handoff's explicit 'do not write tests' instruction): mix test test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs now has 2 pre-existing failures -- both assert the OLD stub error {:error, {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, node_id}} for an :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY node, which REQ-050 legitimately supersedes (a gateway with zero outgoing edges now correctly returns {:error, {:no_matching_edge, node_id, []}} instead). The determinism property test and all other transition_test.exs/variable_merge_test.exs cases still pass unchanged.
